item.title: Single File Library: Major Update
item.content:encoded:
The new update of the Single File Plugin Library solves its two biggest bottlenecks: bandwidth consumption and CPU-heavy boot times.

Instead of downloading and executing the entire TiddlyWiki core to boot the library wiki and using $tw.wiki.getTiddler() for in-memory retrieval, the plugin now uses a zero-boot, byte-slicing approach that drastically cuts bandwidth and memory overhead:

  • A custom saver-hook pre-calculates UTF-8 byte offsets during the wiki save process and appends a compact, cache-busted index to the end of the HTML file.
  • A lightweight injected script intercepts the iframe loading and halts HTML parsing immediately with window.stop(). It replaces the document with an in-memory Blob handler to trigger the onload event and signal that the wiki is ready.
  • The handler fetches an index containing the byte ranges for each plugin and uses it to fetch only the exact byte slices of the specific plugin a user requests (on servers supporting HTTP Range requests). If HTTP Range requests are not supported, it gracefully falls back to buffering the raw text into a local Uint8Array and slices the requested bytes in memory, completely bypassing expensive DOM parsing and core execution.

As a result, the plugin library is faster and lighter. If for any reason you want to download the previous version of the plugin, you can find it here.

item.title: Host-Agnostic Static TiddlyWiki Plugin Library
item.content:encoded:
I have updated the architecture of my TiddlyWiki plugin library to support fully static hosting platforms like GitHub Pages, removing the dependency on server-specific backend endpoints.

Up until now, the plugin library typically relied on Tiddlyhost's JSON endpoints to serve plugin data. This new approach allows a plugin library to run anywhere (GitHub Pages, Tiddlyhost, etc) while maintaining full compatibility with any parent TiddlyWiki instance.

Key Technical Changes

  • Host-Agnostic via postMessage: Communication between the parent wiki and the library iframe uses a secure window.postMessage bridge, allowing the library to be hosted statically without server-side routing.
  • Startup Modules (module-type: startup): The library now uses a native TiddlyWiki startup module instead of manual script injection in the HTML head, ensuring clean execution timing during the boot sequence.
  • In-Memory Retrieval: When a user requests a plugin, the library extracts the tiddler directly from the local in-memory store using $tw.wiki.getTiddler(), avoiding secondary network roundtrips.
  • Native JavaScript Compilation: Metadata, readmes, and icons are processed and serialized in JavaScript. This replaces the previous wikitext macro approach, preventing parsing errors from unescaped quotes or missing SVG namespaces.

item.title: RSS Feed Plugin 0.0.4: Added auto upload feature
item.content:encoded: The RSS Feed plugin now has a Background Actions that check when a tiddler is added or removed from the feed and automatically send the update to github. Note that modifications done to a tiddler are not detected, so if you want to update the feed after editing a tiddler, remember to manually send the feed to github using the button, or let the plugin update the feed when a new tiddler is added or removed from the feed. This feature can be disabled in the plugin settings.

item.title: Announcing the RSS Feed Plugin
item.content:encoded: I am excited to announce the release of a new plugin designed to allow your audience to follow your wiki. This new tool automatically generates a valid RSS 2.0 feed directly from your specified tiddlers and pushes the file from your wiki, straight to GitHub.
